comments.author: Odd-Aside456
comments.body:
Some of the Lego games did this. I don't remember which ones. But I never liked it. It's a really cool idea in theory, but it's dizzying in practice. Not to mention vertical division for 2-player split screen on a 16:9 screen is often not a good idea (I guess it depends on the game), and I just don't think it's a good idea to allow "your side of the screen" to switch.

Some may like it, maybe it's something that can be toggled on in the menu, but I wouldn't make it the default.

I think the only difference in the lego games was that they had an actual division line that would come up when the screens split, I feel like that improves the effect. Also, I think there was some sort of indicator how far you were from the other player? But I could be remembering wrong.

comments.author: Chuckle_Interactive
comments.body:
Some of the games in the Lego series did this (can't find which ones) and I liked it. I think they improved on the technique by:

1. Add a stylized black line along the split just to help it each player see their screen area more clearly. Let it expand into/out of existence so we don't notice it "popping" in.  
2. Let the camera zoom out to try avoiding a split. That also lets you play with the zoom level to hide the transition better.

Overall, I like the feature, I just think it could feel a little more smoother especially when players are so close to each other.
